McLaren.summary: McLaren’s new front‑brake duct smooths the air hitting the front wheels, giving the car a tighter turn‑in and better braking stability on the opening laps. At the rear, a reshaped floor and updated “furniture” under the car boost the low‑down‑force stream, so the chassis sticks to the tarmac more consistently through high‑speed corners. Together they should translate into quicker corner speeds and more confidence for the drivers this weekend.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull has added small winglets to the rear‑wheel area of the car. These extra bits help keep the rear more stable by smoothing out the airflow and reducing wobble at high speeds. The result should be better grip out of fast corners, giving the drivers a little extra confidence and potentially a few tenths of a second over the weekend.

Scuderia Ferrari.summary: Ferrari’s new rear‑corner package now lets the rear tyres stay cooler and more stable, thanks to bigger air inlets, a refined lower deflector and a reshaped wing‑let cluster. In practice, this means the car should grip better out of fast corners and be less prone to overheating, giving the drivers a more consistent feel and potentially stronger lap times this weekend.

Williams Racing.summary: Williams has fitted a freshly shaped front wing, with re‑contoured profiles and re‑engineered endplates to smooth the airflow right off the car. The cleaner‑flow package should give the W14 more front‑end grip, especially in the slower corners where getting the car “on‑track” earlier makes a big difference. In short, the upgrade aims to boost turn‑in stability and overall balance for the upcoming weekend’s race.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Racing Bulls has tweaked the shape of the floor’s edge and the rear diffuser, plus added a new small wing‑like piece ahead of the rear‑corner barge‑board. The changes clean up the airflow under the car and improve rear‑end stability, giving the RB a bit more downforce and grip as they head into the weekend. In plain terms, the car should feel more planted in fast corners and be easier to drive at the limit.

Haas F1 Team.summary: The Haas team has reshaped the rear wing to fine‑tune the downforce it generates, giving the car a more stable feel in high‑speed corners. They’ve also re‑profiled the wing’s endplates to smooth the airflow around the rear, which helps the car stick to the track and improves overall grip. Together, these tweaks should make the car more predictable and quicker through the fast sections of this weekend’s circuit.
